We did it. Hytale is saved. We have acquired Hytale from Riot Games.

Oh and companions might also have their own preferences, which makes most materials still relevant!

Companions are not scheduled for Chapter 2, since it's a lot of work, but they are somewhat working on our dev test environment so we can game-design around them as if they exist and make sure the balance works.

All of the item/crafting changes take a ton of time, but allow us to scale the game "infinitely" and with modders in mind, they can just plug in and add ton without bloating.

There's a lot of itemization/crafting work happening right now, I'm deep in it, and I'm feeling really good about it. We are getting very close to a great balance of being able to add a ton of content without bloating the game, which means we can make a ton of new zones in the future- very exciting future!

Being able to do big chapter drops that comes with items, furniture, blocks and much more will be way easier to implement with these changes and will make new worlds feel fresh every time.

We won't introduce new materials for quite a while, but we do intend to make most armor and weapons relevant throughout the game. 
 
For example, Iron and Adamantite armors will serve different purposes but can be roughly equally strong combat-wise if fully upgraded. While also avoiding making it too good for specific situations and creating a FOMO situation where you feel horrible if you don't have the proper set.

You might not see that in the first pass of itemization, but you could technically upgrade iron armor until it's "as good" as adamantite (it would require quite a lot of materials, including adamantite) and offer a different playstyle / build to the player. For example, socketed gems could behave differently on adamantite armors.

This scales well with cloth/leather armors as well. Some cloth could lean more toward minion bonus amplifications, whereas others could be element-based, and so on. Makes bows/crossbows interesting to add mechanics as well. 

This also means we can spawn players pretty much anywhere in the world, and their environment would dictate their progression a bit more. It also gives players the freedom to create interesting ways to play, every playthrough would be different.

All of this will slowly be introduced and carefully balanced over the months to come. I really want Hytale to be in a position where making a new world feels like a completely new experience every time, which means items, world, explorations, and NPC needs need to be horizontal progression while also offering great verticality to keep players wanting more. Ideally, a top-skilled player can do most content with basic armor/weapons and runes, but we also want the average player to overcome these challenges with some gear upgrades.

I'm a bit of an outsider now, but I can offer some perspective. I have actual numbers and have experienced all of it over my 15-ish years in this business, so maybe that helps you get some context.
First of all, these IRL events basically have negative ROI for player count versus time/money investment, but they do have upsides for making business connections. 

I agree the team could do more in-game events, as we did with Dante, and make overall PVP improvements. That's not off the table. The Dante vs. Technoblade event was massive and is still remembered to this day; this is the kind of good marketing I want to see: the stuff that builds memories.

100% of the "marketing budget" for Hypixel MC is actually creator codes (people like you!). That's why the % is high and has big incentives for players to use it, and some of you are making a better living off this than the YouTube views; we would rather give $ to creators than do traditional marketing, as it would require much more money, people, and so on. The higher the creator code %, the higher the retention is, and the stronger the loop becomes. The best marketing now is to make good content and events, because the creators win massively and so do the players. Good updates = good video = loop

You might think the server could do 3x-5x player count, but the reality is the only way to mathematically achieve this would be to have Bedrock (cross-platform) + AFK mechanics + increase new-player experience to improve early-game retention (this one is planned). There are simply not enough players in Java MC to grab a share of anymore. Unlike Roblox, Minecraft's multiplayer scene is relatively small and split in 2; look at their promoted server experiences on Bedrock, they are doing well, but not Roblox-well, and numerically they do not achieve the Java success (for servers).

I think it's important to look back at all the other MC Java servers and see what history has shown over and over. Only a few are left standing today, and it's true that Hypixel could do better, but it's one of the few that remains; whether you agree with the marketing/updates or not, it has worked out pretty well so far. This year they are seeing growth in term of new players, income and CCU, and they have some exciting things in the works.

Not sure yet if we'll do a big blog post or rely on a trailer for the next chapter (or both). There's so much work happening in parallel right now that it's difficult to predict what will land for CH2 or before. The new crafting progression will definitely require a blog from the designers to explain the long-term vision and "roadmap" so everyone sees why we're making drastic changes.

As we get closer to 1.0, our chapter formula will be easier to maintain with cadence and predictability, since we won't need to touch core gameplay systems much anymore or deal with the domino effects of changes while keeping old crafting/old world gen in mind. At that time, we can just rely on teasers/trailers.
